name: Memphis & Arkansas Bridge
facts: Opened December 17, 1949, the Memphis & Arkansas Bridge became the oldest Interstate bridge in Tennessee and Arkansas, spanning 5,222 feet with five 790‑foot Warren trusses designed by Modjeski and Masters.

The bridge earned National Register of Historic Places status in 2001, yet it lacks the concrete median originally absent, a feature later added to meet Interstate standards and protect the 1940s design.
During the 2021 Hernando de Soto Bridge closure, the Memphis & Arkansas Bridge carried the entire I‑40 detour, highlighting its critical role amid a sudden regional traffic crisis.
